stem.en: Which of the following is NOT regarded as a transition element?

explanation.en: Zn has a completely filled 3d¹⁰ set both as the atom and as Zn²⁺, its only common ion. Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹, so copper counts as a transition metal.

stem.en: The ground-state electronic configuration of chromium (Z = 24) is:

explanation.en: A half-filled 3d⁵ set with 4s¹ is more stable than 3d⁴ 4s², because of exchange energy and symmetry.

stem.en: The general outer electronic configuration of d-block elements is:

explanation.en: The d-block fills the (n−1)d orbitals while ns holds one or two electrons (Pd, 4d¹⁰ 5s⁰, is an exception).

stem.en: The electronic configuration of Cu⁺ (Z of Cu = 29) is:

explanation.en: Cu is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹. Ions lose the 4s electron first, so Cu⁺ is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ (and Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹).

solution.en: Ions lose the 4s electron first, so Cu⁺ is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ (and Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹).

stem.en: Which pair of ions has the same number of 3d electrons?

explanation.en: Mn²⁺ (25 − 2 = 23 e⁻) and Fe³⁺ (26 − 3 = 23 e⁻) are both [Ar] 3d⁵. Fe²⁺ is 3d⁶, Cr³⁺ 3d³, Cu²⁺ 3d⁹, Ni²⁺ 3d⁸.

stem.en: Because of the lanthanoid contraction:

options.en: Zr is much larger than Hf
Zr and Hf have almost the same atomic radius
the 5d metals are much larger than the 4d metals
the 3d and 4d metals have the same radius

explanation.en: The 14 lanthanoids, with their poorly shielding 4f electrons, come before Hf, cancelling the normal increase in size. Zr (160 pm) and Hf (159 pm) are almost equal.

stem.en: Transition metals have high melting points mainly because:

options.en: (n−1)d as well as ns electrons take part in metallic bonding

explanation.en: Many unpaired d electrons add to the metallic bonding, giving high enthalpies of atomisation and high melting points.

stem.en: Which of these 3d metals has the highest third ionisation enthalpy?

explanation.en: Removing a third electron from Mn²⁺ breaks the stable half-filled 3d⁵ set, so Mn has a very high third ionisation enthalpy (about 3248 kJ mol⁻¹).

stem.en: Which 3d metal has the lowest melting point?

explanation.en: Zn (3d¹⁰ 4s²) has no unpaired d electrons for metallic bonding, so its melting point (about 420 °C) is the lowest in the 3d series.

solution.en: Zn (3d¹⁰ 4s²) has no unpaired d electrons for metallic bonding, so its melting point (about 420 °C) is the lowest in the 3d series.

stem.en: Among Cu, Zn, Ni and Fe, the highest second ionisation enthalpy is shown by:

explanation.en: Cu⁺ is 3d¹⁰. Removing an electron from this stable full d set needs a lot of energy (about 1958 kJ mol⁻¹).

stem.en: The highest oxidation state shown by manganese is:

explanation.en: Mn (3d⁵ 4s²) can use all seven outer electrons: +7 in MnO₄⁻ and Mn₂O₇.

stem.en: The only 3d metal with a positive E°(M²⁺/M) value is:

explanation.en: E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V. The high enthalpy of atomisation and ionisation of Cu is not balanced by the hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺, so Cu does not liberate H₂ from dilute acids.

stem.en: Cr²⁺ is a strong reducing agent while Mn³⁺ is a strong oxidising agent, although both are d⁴. This is because:

options.en: Cr is more electronegative than Mn
Cr²⁺ → Cr³⁺ gives stable d³ (t₂g³), and Mn³⁺ → Mn²⁺ gives stable half-filled d⁵

explanation.en: Each ion moves to its more stable configuration: Cr³⁺ (d³, half-filled t₂g level) and Mn²⁺ (d⁵).

stem.en: The oxidation state of chromium in CrO₅ (which has two peroxide groups) is:

explanation.en: CrO₅ has one oxide oxygen (−2) and two O₂²⁻ groups (four O at −1). x − 2 − 4 = 0, so x = +6.

solution.en: CrO₅ has one oxide oxygen (−2) and two O₂²⁻ groups (four O at −1). x − 2 − 4 = 0, so x = +6.

stem.en: Which 3d metal shows only the +3 oxidation state in its compounds?

explanation.en: Sc (3d¹ 4s²) loses all three outer electrons to give the noble-gas Sc³⁺; it shows no other common oxidation state.

stem.en: The spin-only magnetic moment of Mn²⁺ (Z of Mn = 25) is:

explanation.en: Mn²⁺ is 3d⁵ with 5 unpaired electrons: μ = √(5 × 7) = √35 = 5.92 BM.

stem.en: Which of the following ions is colourless in aqueous solution?

explanation.en: Sc³⁺ is 3d⁰: there is no d electron for a d–d transition. Ti³⁺ (d¹), Cu²⁺ (d⁹) and Fe³⁺ (d⁵) are coloured.

stem.en: The catalyst used in the Contact process for making sulphuric acid is:

explanation.en: V₂O₅ catalyses 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃. Iron is used in the Haber process and nickel in hydrogenation of oils.

stem.en: An ion of a 3d metal has a spin-only magnetic moment of 2.84 BM. The ion is:

explanation.en: μ = √(n(n+2)) = 2.84 gives n = 2. Ni²⁺ is 3d⁸ with 2 unpaired electrons. Cr³⁺ has 3, Mn²⁺ 5 and Cu²⁺ 1.

stem.en: Which statement about interstitial compounds of transition metals (such as TiC, Mn₄N, Fe₃H) is NOT correct?

options.en: They are much more reactive than the pure metals

explanation.en: Small atoms such as H, C and N trapped in the metal lattice make the compounds harder and higher melting, still conducting, and chemically inert.

stem.en: When acid is added to a solution of potassium chromate, the colour changes from:

explanation.en: 2CrO₄²⁻ (yellow) + 2H⁺ ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange) + H₂O. Adding alkali reverses the change.

stem.en: In acidic medium, the number of electrons gained by one MnO₄⁻ ion is:

explanation.en: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O: Mn goes from +7 to +2.

stem.en: In neutral or faintly alkaline solution, permanganate is reduced to:

explanation.en: MnO₄⁻ + 2H₂O + 3e⁻ → MnO₂ + 4OH⁻ (Mn +7 → +4).

stem.en: The number of moles of KMnO₄ needed to oxidise one mole of FeSO₄ in acidic medium is:

explanation.en: MnO₄⁻ + 5Fe²⁺ + 8H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + 5Fe³⁺ + 4H₂O. One MnO₄⁻ oxidises five Fe²⁺, so 1 mol Fe²⁺ needs 1/5 = 0.2 mol KMnO₄.

solution.en: One MnO₄⁻ oxidises five Fe²⁺, so 1 mol Fe²⁺ needs 1/5 = 0.2 mol KMnO₄.

stem.en: In acidic medium, one mole of K₂Cr₂O₇ oxidises how many moles of Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺?

explanation.en: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O. Each Fe²⁺ gives one electron, so 6 mol Fe²⁺ are oxidised.

stem.en: The lanthanoid contraction is due to:

options.en: the increase in the number of shells
the imperfect shielding of one 4f electron by another
the decrease in nuclear charge across the series

explanation.en: Each added 4f electron shields the others poorly, so the effective nuclear charge rises steadily and the size falls from La³⁺ to Lu³⁺.

stem.en: The most common oxidation state of the lanthanoids is:

explanation.en: All lanthanoids form Ln³⁺. A few also show +2 (Eu, Yb) or +4 (Ce) when that gives an f⁰, f⁷ or f¹⁴ configuration.

stem.en: Which hydroxide is the least basic?

explanation.en: As the Ln³⁺ ion becomes smaller across the series, the M–OH bond becomes more covalent and the basic character decreases: La(OH)₃ most basic, Lu(OH)₃ least.

stem.en: Which of the following lanthanoid ions is a good oxidising agent in aqueous solution?

explanation.en: Ce⁴⁺ (4f⁰) readily changes to the common +3 state, so it is an oxidant (E°(Ce⁴⁺/Ce³⁺) = +1.74 V). Eu²⁺ and Yb²⁺ change to +3 by losing electrons, so they are reducing agents.

solution.en: Ce⁴⁺ (4f⁰) readily changes to the common +3 state, so it is an oxidant (E°(Ce⁴⁺/Ce³⁺) = +1.74 V).
Eu²⁺ and Yb²⁺ change to +3 by losing electrons, so they are reducing agents.

stem.en: The spin-only magnetic moment of Gd³⁺ (Z of Gd = 64) is about:

explanation.en: Gd is [Xe] 4f⁷ 5d¹ 6s²; Gd³⁺ is 4f⁷ with 7 unpaired electrons. μ = √(7 × 9) = √63 ≈ 7.94 BM.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The E° value of the Mn³⁺/Mn²⁺ couple is much more positive than that of Cr³⁺/Cr²⁺ or Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺.
Reason (R): Mn²⁺ has a particularly stable half-filled 3d⁵ configuration.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Because Mn²⁺ (3d⁵) is especially stable, Mn³⁺ is readily reduced to Mn²⁺, giving a large positive E° (+1.57 V). R explains A.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Cu⁺ is unstable in aqueous solution and disproportionates into Cu²⁺ and Cu.
Reason (R): Cu⁺ has a completely filled 3d¹⁰ configuration.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true, but the instability of Cu⁺(aq) is due to the much larger hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺, which more than compensates its second ionisation enthalpy. The d¹⁰ configuration does not explain it.

passage.en: To find the strength of an iron(II) solution, a student titrates 20.0 mL of acidified ferrous ammonium sulphate solution with 0.020 M KMnO₄. The purple colour of permanganate disappears as each drop is added, until at 25.0 mL a faint pink colour persists. The student adds no separate indicator.

stem.en: What is the molarity of Fe²⁺ in the solution?

passage.en: To find the strength of an iron(II) solution, a student titrates 20.0 mL of acidified ferrous ammonium sulphate solution with 0.020 M KMnO₄. The purple colour of permanganate disappears as each drop is added, until at 25.0 mL a faint pink colour persists. The student adds no separate indicator.

stem.en: Why does the student not need a separate indicator?

options.en: Fe³⁺ formed is deep red and marks the end point
MnO₄⁻ is intensely purple while its product Mn²⁺ is almost colourless, so the first excess drop shows pink
Acid changes colour when Fe²⁺ is used up
KMnO₄ is colourless in acid medium and turns pink in neutral medium

explanation.en: KMnO₄ acts as a self-indicator: while Fe²⁺ remains, purple MnO₄⁻ is reduced to nearly colourless Mn²⁺; one excess drop gives a persistent pink colour.

stem.en: Which of the following ions have a spin-only magnetic moment of about 5.92 BM? One or more options may be correct.

explanation.en: 5.92 BM = √(5 × 7), i.e. five unpaired electrons (d⁵). Mn²⁺ (3d⁵) and Fe³⁺ (3d⁵) have five; Fe²⁺ (3d⁶) has four (4.90 BM) and Cr³⁺ (3d³) has three (3.87 BM).

stem.en: Which statements about potassium permanganate are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.en: In acidic medium MnO₄⁻ accepts five electrons per ion
MnO₄⁻ is paramagnetic because of unpaired d electrons
In neutral or faintly alkaline solution MnO₄⁻ is reduced to MnO₂
The intense purple colour is due to charge transfer, not d–d transitions

explanation.en: Acid: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O. Neutral/faintly alkaline: MnO₄⁻ + 2H₂O + 3e⁻ → MnO₂ + 4OH⁻. Mn(VII) is d⁰, so MnO₄⁻ is diamagnetic and has no d–d transitions; its colour comes from ligand-to-metal charge transfer.

stem.en: Calculate the spin-only magnetic moment of Co²⁺ (Z = 27) in a high-spin state, in BM, to two decimal places.

explanation.en: Co²⁺ is 3d⁷: three unpaired electrons (high spin). μ = √(3 × 5) = √15 = 3.87 BM.

stem.en: What volume (in mL, nearest integer) of 0.025 M KMnO₄ is needed to oxidise 25.0 mL of 0.10 M FeSO₄ in acidic solution?
Which of the following is NOT regarded as a transition element?

explanation.en: A transition element has an incompletely filled d subshell in the atom or in a common ion. Zn is 3d¹⁰ both as the atom and as Zn²⁺; Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹ and Sc is 3d¹.

solution.en: A transition element has an incompletely filled d subshell in the atom or in a common ion.
Zn is 3d¹⁰ both as the atom and as Zn²⁺; Cu²⁺ is 3d⁹ and Sc is 3d¹.

stem.en: The almost identical atomic radii of Zr (160 pm) and Hf (159 pm) are a result of:

explanation.en: Between Zr (4d) and Hf (5d) come the fourteen lanthanoids. Poor shielding by 4f electrons shrinks the atoms, cancelling the size increase expected for the next shell.

solution.en: Between Zr (4d) and Hf (5d) come the fourteen lanthanoids.
Poor shielding by 4f electrons shrinks the atoms, cancelling the size increase expected for the next shell.

stem.en: Given E°(M³⁺/M²⁺): Cr −0.41 V, Mn +1.57 V, Fe +0.77 V, Co +1.97 V. Which M²⁺ ion is the strongest reducing agent?

explanation.en: The most negative E°(M³⁺/M²⁺) means M²⁺ is most easily oxidised to M³⁺. Cr²⁺ (−0.41 V) → Cr³⁺ (stable t₂g³) is the strongest reducing agent.
